contests.seatContext: Cornyn seeking 5th term (first elected 2002). Texas has not elected a Democrat to U.S. Senate since 1992. Facing the most expensive Senate primary in history — over $110M in total ad spend as of Feb 25, 2026, driven heavily by $57M+ in outside spending backing Cornyn. Runoff very likely on Republican side given three-way race with no candidate polling near 50%.
contests.raceRatingSource: Cook Political Report / Inside Elections / Sabato's Crystal Ball (all three in agreement)

candidates.priorOffice: Texas Attorney General (1999-2002); Texas Supreme Court Justice (1991-1997)
candidates.notes: Vulnerable incumbent — underwater in favorability at -8 among Republican primary voters. Attacked by Paxton and Hunt as insufficiently conservative, particularly over his 2022 bipartisan gun safety bill. Campaign message centers on '99.2% voting record with President Trump.' Massive cash-on-hand advantage ($11.2M raised; allied super PACs have spent ~$57M). Runoff widely expected if he cannot clear 50% on March 3.

candidates.priorOffice: Texas State Representative (2003-2012); Texas State Senator (2013-2015)
candidates.fundraisingTrend: Declining each quarter — $2.9M Q2 2025, $1.3M Q3 2025, $1.1M Q4 2025

alternatePolling.note: Led in this poll with Cornyn at 31%, Hunt at 17%

candidates.notes: Running as the hard-right challenger to Cornyn. Survived 2023 impeachment acquittal by Texas Senate. Favorability underwater at -10 among Republican primary voters. Fundraising has weakened significantly each quarter but holds ~$3.7M cash on hand. Positions himself as 'battle-tested' conservative who will 'take a sledgehammer to the D.C. establishment.' Widely expected to be in the runoff. Announced candidacy April 8, 2025.

candidates.priorOffice: U.S. Army (Apache helicopter pilot, West Point graduate)
candidates.notes: Entered race October 6, 2025, as the youngest of the three front-runners. Narrows positive favorability among Republican primary voters — the only top-tier candidate not underwater. Running on 'next generation' and 'America First' messaging. Has faced scrutiny for missed House votes during the Senate campaign. Seen as the potential spoiler or runoff wild card. Gave up TX-38 seat to run.

candidates.priorOffice: Texas State Representative (2021-2023); public defender; civil rights attorney
candidates.fundraisingNote: Majority transferred from House campaign account after late entry (December 8, 2025)

alternatePolling.note: Trailed Talarico 47-38 in this earlier poll

candidates.notes: National profile as vocal progressive House member; frequent cable news presence. Entered race December 8, 2025, three months after Talarico. Late entry initially allowed Talarico to lead in early polls, but most recent UT poll shows Crockett ahead by double digits (56-44). Endorsed by EMILY's List. Gave up TX-30 seat to run. Campaign message focuses on affordability.

candidates.priorOffice: Middle school teacher; Presbyterian seminary student
candidates.fundraisingNote: Leads entire Texas Senate field in fundraising on Democratic side — $20.7M raised. Does not accept corporate PAC money.

alternatePolling.note: Led Crockett 47-38 in this earlier poll

candidates.notes: Announced September 9, 2025 — three months before Crockett. Massive fundraising advantage over the entire Democratic field at $20.7M raised. Runs explicitly anti-corporate-PAC campaign; 'top vs. bottom' economic framing. Sweeps major Texas newspaper endorsements. Strong early polling lead has narrowed as Crockett entered and gained momentum. Progressive state legislator running a grassroots-style campaign.
Third Democratic primary candidate. No FEC filings found, minimal public profile, 1% in polling. Included on ballot but does not meet viability threshold. No campaign website confirmed.

ballotMeasures.officialTitle: Texas Republican Primary Advisory Propositions (10 questions)
ballotMeasures.yesVoteMeans: Voter endorses the stated party platform position (non-binding — results have no legal effect)
ballotMeasures.noVoteMeans: Voter does not endorse the stated party platform position
ballotMeasures.summary: Texas Republicans will vote on 10 non-binding advisory questions including: property tax phase-out via purchase-price assessment, requiring voter approval for local tax increases, banning healthcare denial based on vaccination status, requiring schools to teach life begins at fertilization, banning gender/sexuality clinics in K-12 schools, term limits on elected officials, prohibiting large-scale groundwater export, ending public services for undocumented immigrants, barring Democrats from legislative leadership roles, and prohibiting Sharia law.

ballotMeasures.officialTitle: Texas Democratic Primary Advisory Propositions (13 questions)
ballotMeasures.yesVoteMeans: Voter endorses the stated party platform position (non-binding — results have no legal effect)
ballotMeasures.noVoteMeans: Voter does not endorse the stated party platform position
ballotMeasures.summary: Texas Democrats will vote on 13 non-binding advisory questions emphasizing healthcare expansion (Medicaid), reproductive healthcare access, education funding, immigration reform, voting rights access, and anti-gerrymandering/redistricting reform including creation of a nonpartisan redistricting board.

ballotMeasures.yesVoteMeans: TBD — Texas Legislature has not yet passed amendments for the November 2026 ballot
ballotMeasures.summary: Texas voters approved all 17 constitutional amendments on the November 2025 ballot. The 90th Texas Legislature regular session began January 2025. Any constitutional amendments for November 2026 would need to be passed by the legislature; specific measures have not yet been certified as of February 2026. This entry should be updated once the legislative session concludes.
